- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns bullish after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope gently.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model should not overreact to short-term volatility.
- If model forecast is >+10% above recent 18-day average, flag for overconfidence; reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” values, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >+5% above model, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if yes, model may have missed momentum.
